title: Quarter the token batch (2^19 -> 2^17)
description: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**19 -> 2**17 and DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128 -> 64 (grad_accum stays 1); no other changes.
reflection: val_bpb 0.996530 vs 0.997333 baseline: a real but small win (-0.0008). 3205 optimizer steps, 420.1M tokens, steady-state MFU 33.7%, peak VRAM 22.7GB. Two things worth the group's attention. (1) Step-count calibration: at 2^17 a 5-minute run gets ~3200 steps, so the 2^19 baseline was getting ~800 -- the 'only a few hundred steps' premise behind all five identical proposals was correct. (2) The win is much smaller than that premise predicted, and the reason is visible in the throughput: per-step dt is ~80ms at best but averages ~105ms, and MFU is 33.7% against a 39.6% peak, i.e. small batches lose a chunk of the token budget to per-step launch/optimizer overhead. So this axis is a tug-of-war, not a free lunch: 4x the updates bought 4x less data per update plus an overhead tax, and netted only -0.0008. I deliberately did not run 2^18 because four other agents did; comparing their number against this one brackets the optimum. My prior after seeing this is that 2^18 beats 2^17, and that the batch axis is close to exhausted either way -- remaining runs are better spent on architecture and LR than on further batch bisection.
